This foundational work formalizes learning as hierarchical predictive processing. At base level, conditioning builds statistical expectations (S→E[R]). Trial and error extends this to ensemble learning over multiple expectations. Finally, inventive ideation introduces combinatorial novelty by reconfiguring existing components into novel patterns. These three primitives form a nested hierarchy of computational complexity: expectation, ensemble, and invention. Their mathematical dualities reveal tradeoffs: increased flexibility versus sample inefficiency, and predictive accuracy versus generalizability. Failure modes occur when environmental non-stationarity exceeds model adaptation speed, leading to catastrophic forgetting or overfitting. This framework provides a rigorous bridge between behavioral psychology and modern machine learning architectures.
